native_result.query: How does age influence the likelihood of withdrawing more money from savings than putting in?
native_result.HypoA: Younger individuals are more likely to withdraw more money from savings than they had put in and with a negative coefficient between age and withdrawing more than putting into savings (-0.0422).
native_result.WorkflowA:
1. One-hot encode Gender variable into MALE and FEMALE
2. Extract the independent variables ['AGE','INCOME', 'BMI', 'BLACK', 'HISPANIC', 'MALE', 'FEMALE']
3. Add dependent variable (DISSAVED) from the df
4. Add a constant term to the independent variable to account for the intercept term in the logistic regression model.
5. Fit a logistic regression model
native_result.HypoB: Age is negatively associated with the likelihood of withdrawing more money from savings than putting in (dissaving), with the odds of dissaving decreasing by approximately 4.1% per year of age (AME = -0.76 percentage points per year, p < 0.001), reflecting a decrease in the rate of time preference as young adults mature from their mid-twenties into their early thirties.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Preprocessed NLSY79 data, created gender indicator and identified mean-imputed income and BMI records. 2. Estimated univariate and multivariable Logit models (linear and quadratic age specifications). 3. Estimated Linear Probability Models with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors (HC1). 4. Computed average marginal effects (AME) and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. 5. Performed sensitivity checks on log-transformed income and complete-case subsamples. 6. Synthesized findings into a formal hypothesis contextualized by time preference theory.

sub_hypo.text: Younger individuals are more likely to withdraw more money from savings than they put in, with an age coefficient of -0.0422 in the logistic regression.
sub_hypo.context: Respondents in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79), with age measured in 1989.
sub_hypo.relations: AGE has a negative logistic regression coefficient of -0.0422 for DISSAVED = 1 (withdrawing more money from savings than putting in), controlling for INCOME, BMI, BLACK, HISPANIC, and gender encoded as MALE and FEMALE. Younger respondents are more likely to dissave.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Younger individuals are more likely to withdraw more money from savings than they had put in and with a negative coefficient between age and withdrawing more than putting into savings (-0.0422).

sub_hypo.text: Age is negatively associated with dissaving among young adults, with the odds of dissaving decreasing by approximately 4.1% per year of age (AME = -0.76 percentage points per year, p < 0.001), reflecting a decrease in the rate of time preference as they mature from their mid-twenties into their early thirties.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 respondents maturing from their mid-twenties into their early thirties, contextualized by time preference theory.
sub_hypo.relations: Increasing age is associated with a lower likelihood of withdrawing more money from savings than putting in: approximately 4.1% lower odds per additional year of age and an average marginal effect of -0.76 percentage points per year (p < 0.001).
